clue.text: George, 8, is not used to land, of course

definitions.text: George, 8, is not used to land, of course

parts.words: George, 8, is not used to land, of course
parts.note: George is the old pilots' nickname for the automatic flying system; 8 points to 8 down, meaning 'people claim', and an aircraft's crew switch it off for landing

explanation.surface: A man named George, introduced by hearsay, apparently never comes ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 8 as its answer at 8 down ('people claim') and the clue says: George, people claim, is not used for landing. The cross-reference makes George look like a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots have long called the autopilot 'George', and it is normally disengaged before the plane touches down.

clue.text: Stranger's right to support Central council woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the right-hand letter goes below the woman
central picks the three letters at the heart of the word council

parts.note: Annie is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A strange council member's rights are backed by central government, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central council' takes the middle three letters UNC; 'to support' puts R under ANNIE, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger here is the comparative adjective, more weird or eerie, matching the comparative form.

clue.text: The vitality of ducks on speed

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, written O, so two ducks are two Os
speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: Racing ducks show plenty of life.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket, so it gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for energy and liveliness, a close synonym of vigour.

clue.text: Past heads of department aren't really keen on nights

parts.note: past means after, as in 'past midnight'

indicators.note: heads of takes the first letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Former department managers are not fond of working night shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done after dark happens in the night-time hours, the time of working nights.

clue.text: Popular eastern exercise that's useless

parts.note: popular things are said to be in
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A trendy Eastern workout regime turns out to be worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone useless at a task is clumsy and incompetent, a synonym.

clue.text: Roam around in alarm that's universal

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for alarm

parts.note: alarm is panic, sudden fear

indicators.note: around signals the letters of roam moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Wandering about in a state of fright felt like a cosmic experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarm' looks like part of the scene but supplies the container; 'around' scrambles the first word, and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in everything all around, so it is all-encompassing, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Daniel stupidly ignores one so gets charged

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters of Daniel are jumbled foolishly into a new order
ignores tells us that one letter of the name is left out of the jumble

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A foolish Daniel overlooks someone and ends up facing a criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I ('one', which 'ignores' drops) from DANIEL and 'stupidly' rearranges the rest into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charged in the sense of loaded or filled up, as a weighted cart or a gun is.

clue.text: Easy solution is within your grasp, people claim

indicators.note: is within places the rearranged letters inside the old word for your
grasp shows the outer word holding the shuffled letters in its hold

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

indicators.note: solution signals a dissolving and remaking of the letters of easy

explanation.surface: Supporters say the answer is easy to reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution' is the anagram signal, not an answer to a problem; 'your' is the archaic form, and 'is within' and 'grasp' both say it holds the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces hearsay: it is what people say or allege, a set idiom.

clue.text: Minister is just semi-employed by Uncle Richard

indicators.note: only part of the words uncle and Richard is used, so the letters sit hidden across them

explanation.surface: A churchman works part-time for his uncle Richard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-employed' looks like a job description, but it says only parts of 'Uncle Richard' are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Not well treated by this deputy?

definitions.text: Not well treated by this deputy?

parts.words: Not well treated by this deputy?
parts.note: a stand-in doctor treats patients who are not well while the usual doctor is away

explanation.surface: Someone feels poorly served by a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not well treated' sounds like a complaint, but it means the sick are treated by this deputy.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a temporary doctor or clergyman covering for an absent colleague, so a deputy.

clue.text: Draw then colour, a dying art you might say

definitions.text: a dying art you might say

parts.note: a drawn game is a tie
then can mean and, as in 'this and that'
to colour fabric is to dye it

explanation.surface: Sketch, then paint: a craft on its way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dying art' is a pun: a dyeing art, not one fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a method of patterning cloth by knotting it before dyeing, so an art of dyeing, punned as dying.

clue.text: He has spread out in the West

definitions.text: He has spread out in the West

parts.words: He has spread out in the West
parts.note: a spread is an American word for a large farm, and the man who owns one out West is the clue's subject

explanation.surface: A man has sprawled out, or expanded, somewhere in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' is a noun here, a big American farm, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle farmer in the American West owns a spread, a large stock farm.

clue.text: Special chairs featured in popular TV drama

definitions.text: Special chairs featured in popular TV drama

parts.words: Special chairs featured in popular TV drama
parts.note: royal seats, and the last word of the title of the fantasy series Game of ...

explanation.surface: Furniture used as props in a hit television series.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal seats are ceremonial chairs, and the word ends the TV fantasy series title Game of ...

clue.text: Scale devised by leading club member

indicators.note: leading takes the first letter of the word club

parts.note: a limb such as an arm or leg is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A grading scale is drawn up by a prominent club member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like a noun for a grading system, but it is the verb, to ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or peak is to ascend it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Accept my word (though it conceals a lie!)

definitions.text: Accept my word (though it conceals a lie!)

parts.words: Accept my word (though it conceals a lie!)
parts.note: a plea to be trusted, whose first word happens to contain the letters of a falsehood

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be trusted while admitting they are not quite honest.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket points out that the first word of the phrase literally contains the letters L-I-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase asks the listener to trust the speaker, to take their word for it.

clue.text: Play with a hundred actors working together

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a company is a troupe of actors who perform together

explanation.surface: A drama performed by a hundred-strong troupe of cooperating actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a stage play, but 'Play with' means to perform musically alongside someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany a singer is to play music along with them, a synonym.

clue.text: Vicar with hair restyled for noisy wedding party

indicators.note: restyled, as a hairdo is, says the letters of vicar and hair are rearranged

explanation.surface: The vicar gets a new hairdo for a rowdy wedding celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a mock serenade with pots and pans for newlyweds, a raucous folk custom.

clue.text: A national broadcast concerning Asia Minor

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of a national are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A national radio programme covers the region of Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolia is the old name for Asia Minor, the Turkish peninsula, and the adjective describes its people or things.

clue.text: Succeed really well at cleaning job with Mike

parts.note: toiling hard at domestic cleaning is to labour as a charlady would, char being British for a cleaner
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone does very well in a cleaning post alongside a colleague called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is British for a paid house cleaner; to labour as one is to slog, and adding M finishes the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be extremely effective, as if by magic.

clue.text: Parry's in hospital unit, unwell

parts.note: a ward is a room or unit in a hospital
feeling off means slightly ill

explanation.surface: A man called Parry is in a hospital ward, feeling ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parry' reads as a surname, but it is the fencing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To parry a blow is to deflect or fend it off, an equivalent phrase.

clue.text: See 19
Mouser's flair, oddly, for finding food …

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on, of the words

explanation.surface: A cat's talent for sniffing out something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This breakfast cereal of oats, nuts and dried fruit is a kind of food.

clue.text: In common parlance they chase police, inappropriately!

definitions.text: In common parlance they chase police, inappropriately!

parts.words: In common parlance they chase police, inappropriately!
parts.note: in the phrase 'cops and ...' the thieves seem to follow the police, the wrong way round from real life

explanation.surface: A grumble that a familiar saying gets pursuit backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In the children's game 'cops and ...' the criminals come after the police in the words, though police chase criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves who steal are what the police pursue, so the clue's 'they' are criminals.

clue.text: … and achieves success by bringing it home

definitions.text: … and achieves success by bringing it home

parts.words: … and achieves success by bringing it home
parts.note: the idiom 'bring home the ...' means to earn a living or succeed, and the missing word is also food, continuing the previous clue

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a cat succeeds by carrying its catch home.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 21 down, where 'food' was the definition; this one is also a food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing home the cured pork is the idiom for earning money or winning.

clue.text: A raised place is said to prevent slouching

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: An elevated spot is supposed to stop people slumping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PUTIS upwards in this down entry. The definition is the command itself: what is said to someone slumping.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the instruction a teacher or parent gives to make someone straighten their back.

clue.text: What petitioners do with one politician's knowledge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: People lobbying use a single MP's expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Petitioners beg or beseech those in power, which is a synonym for pleading.

clue.text: It goes after seed like a bird

indicators.note: goes after puts the word it behind the word for seed

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

explanation.surface: Something chases after birdseed the way a bird would.
explanation.definitionFit: This small brown songbird, related to wagtails, is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Horse and cart transported some players

indicators.note: transported means carried off, so the letters of horse and cart are carried into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A horse and cart carried a few performers.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of musicians, so a group of players.

clue.text: Sounds like smooth little glass bottle

indicators.note: sounds like says the word for smooth is heard, not spelt

parts.note: to file something is to smooth it with a rasp

explanation.surface: A small bottle of smooth glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial or small medicine bottle, the old spelling with PH.

clue.text: Digitally generated artwork

parts.note: digitally sounds like computer art, but it means made with the digits, the fingers

explanation.surface: A piece of computer art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digitally' means with the fingers, not by computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's picture made by daubing paint with the fingers is literally digit-made art.
